extracted.intended_audience: extramural grantee institution staff (PD/PIs, Signing Officials (SO), Grants Management Specialists, institutional administrators) who use eRA Commons
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and mandatory requirements for completing NIH grant administration tasks in eRA Commons: submitting Final Progress Reports, FRAM responses, Just-In-Time materials, No-Cost Extension requests, Relinquishing Statements (Change of Institution), and related electronic workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report minimum content
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, the Final Progress Report should include: a statement of progress made towards the originally stated aims; a list of results (positive and/or negative) considered significant; a list of publications resulting from the project (including plans for further publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of reprints or publications not previously submitted should accompany the Final Progress Report. If publications are in PubMed Central (PMC), the PMC submission ID may be included instead of a hard copy. Also include reports on gender and minority subject inclusion (using PHS2590 table), indication of children’s involvement or relevance to children, and description of data/materials/protocols/software available for sharing and access methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Progress Report format requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Progress Report must be uploaded in Adobe PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Closeout - Upload Final Progress Report screen to choose and submit the PDF. After saving, status updates to Received and only a View FPR link remains. If additional information is requested by the Program Officer, use FRAM functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM purpose and triggering condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM) are requested by a Program Officer when additional materials related to a submitted Final Progress Report are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When PO requests FRAM, PI is notified via email, Closeout Status updates to 'FRAM Requested', and a FRAM Update link appears for uploading the additional material.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM upload file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: FRAM attachments must be in PDF format and no larger than 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Add Attachment button on the FRAM screen to select and upload. After passing system validations, message displays that FRAM was successfully uploaded and is ready for SO processing. Attachments can be viewed or deleted prior to submission to Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM upload and edit responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI is responsible for uploading requested FRAM attachments; the SO (Signing Official) is responsible for submitting FRAM to the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI uploads via FRAM Update link; multiple uploads append to the stored PDF. Before SO submission, PI-uploaded attachments can be deleted. Only users with SO role can submit FRAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM submission certification and immutability
rubrics_metrics.description: When SO submits FRAM, a certification is required and FRAM cannot be edited after submission to Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After SO submission, Closeout Status shows 'FRAM Submitted By <SO Name>' and FRAM Update link is replaced by View FRAM. Commons generates a combined PDF containing all FRAM documents accessible in Status Information. Note: PO may rescind approval of the Final Progress Report submission at any time; if rescinded, FRAM Update link may be re-enabled.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM post-submission additions (before acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: SOs can continue to add additional attachments after submission to Agency but before acceptance of the FPR; subsequent documents are appended to the generated PDF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although SO can add attachments after submission, FRAM cannot be edited after SO submits to Agency in the sense that the FRAM Update link is replaced by View FRAM once submitted; the guide notes SOs can continue to add attachments even after submission to Agency (before acceptance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Just-In-Time (JIT) purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT allows electronic submittal of additional application information after peer review and prior to funding, when requested by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit JIT information until specifically requested (system-generated emails or direct contacts). JIT generally becomes available for applications within a certain percentile/priority score range; JIT policy details are in the NIH Grants Policy Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT allowed document types
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT accepts uploads for: Other Support File, Budget Upload, Other Upload, Human Subject Education, Genome Data Sharing Certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other Support should include active and pending support for key personnel (financial resources in direct support, excluding training awards/prizes/gifts). If animals/humans involved, IACUC/IRB date and assurance number verification required on the JIT screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT file format and size
rubrics_metrics.description: All JIT attachments should be submitted in PDF format with a maximum size of 6MB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Upload/Choose File/Upload File buttons on the Just In Time screen. Commons performs validations upon saving and submission and displays error messages if required information is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support content/format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Support should report active and pending support for key personnel and include all financial resources in direct support of research endeavors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested format available at the provided URL (othersupport.doc); upload that file using the Import button. Training awards, prizes, or gifts need not be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT submission authority and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs may upload and save JIT information, but only users with SO role can submit JIT information to NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After saving, SO sees Submit enabled and validations occur on save and submit. JIT link is removed once an application is awarded. Each JIT section can be submitted separately and more than once if at least one field element is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT resubmission and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: JIT information can be resubmitted as many times as necessary; the Number of Submissions for each piece of information is tracked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status result screens display JIT link with an indication of how many times revised. View Just In Time Report to review before submitting; if submitted to NIH, the report is accessible via Status Information under Other Relevant Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Cost Extension (NCE) eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantee may extend the final budget period one time for up to 12 months without additional NIH funds if: (1) no additional funds are required by NIH, and (2) there will be no change in the project's originally approved scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere presence of remaining funds at grant expiration is insufficient justification for an NCE. Extensions beyond the one-time 12 months require prior NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Cost Extension allowable justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: An NCE may be granted when: additional time is required to complete the originally approved project; continuity of NIH support is needed while a competing continuation application is under review; or extension is necessary to permit orderly phase-out of a project that will not receive continued support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the number of months (one-month increments up to 12) in Commons. The link to request NCE is available 90 days before project end and removed at midnight on project end date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-Cost Extension mandatory electronic submission via Commons
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires grantees to request NCE through the eRA Commons No-Cost Extension feature; NIH will not accept notification via other channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an internal business error prevents processing, status displays as 'Extension Error' with instructions for whom to contact. Once corrected, appropriate eNotifications are sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Institution (Relinquishing Statement) purpose and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Relinquishing Statements (RS) electronically relinquish interests and rights to PHS research grants and typically accompany a change of institution or successor-in-interest request; RS must be completed before expiration of the approved project period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving institution must submit an application via Grants.gov using the Parent FOA. This electronic RS process is an open pilot and may be used instead of traditional paper processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of Institution eligible/ineligible grants
rubrics_metrics.description: All awarded and active grants are eligible to be relinquished except those with statuses: 02 Withdrawn; 21 Ineligible organization - application withdrawn; 30 Withdrawn by IC; 34 Administratively withdrawn by IC prior to review or council. Subprojects, Institutional Allowances, and Supplements are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RS(s) may be submitted for any activity code otherwise eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement access & submission authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Only users with SO authority at the grantee (relinquishing) institution can access the Change of Institution option and submit the RS to the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PI can access and edit limited fields (New Institution Name and Contact information) when they are the current reviewer. Internal NIH users and Grants Management Officials have specific view/update/receive/return permissions as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement required fields and form completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Required fields on the RS include: New Institution Name, Contact Email at the Institution, Requested Termination Date (MMDDYYYY), and Direct Cost $.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete New Institution Name via search to populate DUNS/IPF if possible; type NONE in Equipment Transferring with the Project if no equipment to transfer. Save sets status to SO Work in Progress. New Institution data is validated upon routing by the PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement validation and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The RS is validated upon submitting to the Agency. The RS cannot be submitted with validation errors but may be submitted with validation warnings. Saving does not execute validations. PD/PI verification is not required to submit; SO can submit without routing to PD/PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RS(s) submitted for pre-award are not validated for costs relinquished and can be zero or original application amounts. New institution data validation occurs on routing by PD/PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement routing order and edit flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The next reviewer defaults to the contact PD/PI on the application; current user is not shown as next reviewer. If SO is current, PD/PI is next; if PD/PI is current reviewer, the initiating SO is first default entry, others listed alphabetically. RS can be routed back and forth between SO and PD/PI unlimited times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of valid next reviewers shows Name (LAST, FIRST). Screens are named appropriately (Route to PD/PI or Route to SO) depending on direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing Statement business rules (multiple submissions, deletion, visibility, timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple RS submissions are allowed. SO can submit a new RS only if no RS has been submitted or existing RS(s) have been acknowledged (Accepted for Consideration or Refused). RS can be deleted if in SO Work in Progress and never submitted. All submitted and accepted RS versions are visible to receiving institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant applications for the new institution should be submitted within 30 days after the Relinquishing Statement is submitted from the former institution. The Relinquishing Statement should be submitted within 30 days of the grant application for the new institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishing SO responsibilities for RS creation/editing
rubrics_metrics.description: The SO at the original grantee institution initiates the RS and can Start, View, Edit, Save, Route, Cancel, Delete and Submit RS to Agency; SO must complete required fields and perform the search/insert steps for New Institution Name/IPF/DUNS as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To start an RS, use Change of Institution link on Commons Status, search by Institution Code and Serial Number, Manage Relinquishing Statement, then Start a new RS. Save sets status to SO Work in Progress. If award is in NCE or within 3 months of end date, an informational pop-up appears advising to contact awarding IC because IC policies may limit transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR module functional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPR module allows electronic initiation, routing for institutional review/approval, viewing routing history, error checking, electronic submission of Research Performance Progress Reports, and storage of a generated PDF in the electronic grant folder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SO may delegate authority to PD/PI for submitting an RPPR. A detailed RPPR instruction guide is available online for field-by-field guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Assisted Review (IAR) reviewer functions
rubrics_metrics.description: IAR provides a standard process for Reviewers to submit critiques, preliminary and final scores, and to view grant applications and meeting materials via Commons; reviewers may view others’ critiques before the meeting unless conflicts exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IAR online help is available to users with IAR roles; currently aimed at Reviewers. IAR expedites review meetings by enabling more informed discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: xTrain access roles
rubrics_metrics.description: xTrain module provides online capabilities for trainee appointments and terminations; accessible to roles: TRAINEE, PI, SO, BO, SPONSOR, and ASST (when delegated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: xTrain has its own online help and references relevant policies (Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA and reporting/assurance requirements for training awards).
